children: Kenya and Rwanda signed 11 bilateral agreements and Memoranda of Understanding in Nairobi to expand strategic cooperation and economic ties.
The agreements were concluded on Tuesday following the 10th Session of the Kenya-Rwanda Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation (JPCC).

They were co-chaired by Kenya’s Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, Dr Musalia Mudavadi, and Rwanda’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Dr Usta Kaitesi.

The cooperation includes agreements on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters and the transfer of sentenced persons, alongside MoUs on political consultations, immigration, housing and urban development, diaspora management, water resources and irrigation, and local governance.
The two governments committed to facilitating the movement of goods and services, increasing investment and strengthening business-to-business links.
The Northern Corridor, which connects Rwanda to the Port of Mombasa remains a key transit corridor for the two countries.

They also include importation of crude oil and its transport along the Northern Corridor, cooperation between Rwanda Investigation Bureau and Kenya National Police Service, culture and heritage, and conservation.
The cooperation covers areas ranging from mutual legal assistance and the transfer of sentenced persons to police cooperation, immigration, local governance and political consultations.

Mudavadi said the JPCC provides a mechanism for translating political commitments between Nairobi and Kigali into practical cooperation.“The 10th Session of the JPCC provides an important platform for our two governments to review progress, strengthen follow-up on agreed commitments, address outstanding matters and identify new opportunities for cooperation,” Mudavadi said.

On trade and investment, the two countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral economic relations, facilitating the movement of goods and services and promoting greater investment flows between the two countries.
They further encouraged increased private-sector engagement and business-to-business linkages.

Kaitesi said the commission was important in turning the two countries’ political relationship into concrete action.“Kenya remains one of Rwanda’s key economic partners in the region. A number of Kenyan companies have invested and established a strong presence in Rwanda, particularly in the service sector, including Kenya Commercial Bank and Equity Bank. At the same time, Rwandan companies continue to explore and expand opportunities in the Kenyan Market,” said Kaitesi.“Trade is also an important pillar of our economic relations. Our bilateral trade continues to benefit from our geographical proximity, strong business linkages, and shared commitment to regional economic integration through the East African Community.”In 2025, Rwanda imported goods worth over $398 million from Kenya, while exports to Kenya were valued at $5.3 million. “These figures reflect the strong standing and growing commercial ties between our two countries and the significant potential for expanding further our bilateral trade.”On transport, infrastructure, and energy, the two EAC partner states underscored the importance of strengthening regional connectivity and welcomed continued cooperation under the Northern Corridor. Kaitesi described the shipment of crude oil along the Northern Corridor as an important step in strengthening Rwanda’s energy security and said Kigali would continue working with Nairobi to ensure the bulk petroleum procurement route provides reliable and secure supplies.
They further agreed to enhance technical cooperation in areas of mutual interest, including geothermal energy, housing and urban development, infrastructure development, and transport logistics.

Among the agreements is a new Memorandum of Understanding between the Rwanda Investigation Bureau and the Kenya National Police Service, providing a framework for closer cooperation between the two countries’ law-enforcement agenciesThe agreements include expanded transport logistics, petroleum and water management, housing and urban development, plus ongoing Northern Corridor integration (including the KPA liaison office in Kigali and Naivasha dry port arrangements).

At the continental level, Kenya and Rwanda have also been strong advocates of reforms within the African Union aimed at making the African Union Commission more effective, fit for purpose, and better able to serve the interest of African citizens.
The next 11th Session of the Kenya–Rwanda Joint Permanent Commission for Cooperation (JPCC) will be held in Rwanda in 2028, on dates to be mutually agreed through diplomatic channels.
